title: EMERGENCY EPISODE: Safe SuperIntelligence and Claude 3.5 Sonnet
description: Send us Fan Mail Just a few days after we recorded our podcast re-launch and Matt's 'Call to Arms' on mitigating the risks of development of AI, llya Sutskever emerged from the wilderness. He announced, with very few details, the founding of Safe SuperIntelligence, with the implicit mission to build Superintelligent AI aligned with human values, to prevent catastrophic outcomes for humanity. In our first ever EMERGENCY EPISODE we dissect this potentially seismic disruption in the AI landscape. After a failed coup against Sam Altman led to his exit from OpenAI, Sutskever is now on a mission to create ASI that prioritizes humanity's welfare. We navigate the complexities of this new direction and reflect on the ethical conundrums that lie ahead, especially in contrast to OpenAI's transformation from a non-profit to a for-profit juggernaut. Is Ilya the new Effective Alturism hero? or just the lastest AI expert to decide to do 'The Worst Thing Possible'? But that's not all—meet Claude 3.5, Anthropic's latest large language model that’s setting unprecedented benchmarks. From improved coding capabilities to multimodal functionalities, Claude 3.5 is a game-changer for both developers and casual users. We’ll also explore the UK's pioneering steps in AI safety through the UK Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute (AISI), and dive into a provocative paper by Glasgow University scholars that questions the factual reliability of models like ChatGPT. This episode promises a riveting discussion on the future of AI, safety, and the pursuit of truth in a digital age. Hicks et al (2024)- ChatGPT is Bullshit ChatGPT is bullshit | Ethics and Information Technology (springer.com) Introducing Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Pascal Biese) 🤔 Has OpenAI Lost Its Edge? - by Pascal Biese - LLM Watch
summary: The first 'emergency episode' responds to Ilya Sutskever founding Safe Superintelligence days after their relaunch call-to-arms: Matt wants to believe Ilya but questions how safety-first wins an ASI race against investor pressure, quoting Zvi Moshkowitz's 'worst possible thing' critique. They also cover Claude 3.5 Sonnet topping benchmarks at a fifth of Opus's cost, the UK AISI's pre-release safety evaluation, and the Glasgow paper arguing ChatGPT is 'bullshit'.
keyTalkingPoints: SSI aims for a 'straight shot' to safe ASI — but you cannot reach ASI without passing AGI, and alignment of a superintelligence may be impossible
Matt believes Ilya is genuine but 'Sam Altman is now the devil'; trillion-dollar compute needs will let investors tip the balance
Zvi Moshkowitz quote: Ilya is 'the latest to do the worst possible thing', calling it 'safe' is not an improvement
Claude 3.5 Sonnet beats Opus and GPT-4o across benchmarks while faster and roughly five times cheaper; best-in-class vision
UK AISI ran a pre-release safety evaluation — Britain is 'walking the walk' on governance and pressures OpenAI to follow
Hicks et al (Glasgow): LLMs produce 'soft bullshit' (no concern for truth) and maybe 'hard bullshit' (designed to seem truth-seeking)

jimmy: Most curious how SSI could technically make a superintelligence safe — a truly superhuman system would have something like free will
If SSI succeeds it may force OpenAI to put safety back on the agenda; the announcement keeps safety in the headlines either way
Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the best model right now — Anthropic is superseding OpenAI in quality, speed and cost
The 'ChatGPT is bullshit' paper is welcome coping — LLMs are not as advanced as their makers claim
matt: Torn: believes Ilya's intentions but thinks investor pressure will eventually corrupt any safety-first ASI venture
The real positive is narrative — the industry's top technical mind putting safety first legitimizes the whole governance agenda
Anthropic has taken the ethical seat OpenAI vacated; SSI adds a player and decentralizes power in the race
Quotes Zvi's pessimistic take and demands substance: 'How is he going to make it safe? His statements tell us nothing'
